summary: Nacogdoches County, TX Texas Forest Service fire tower listed as gone; a 1948 survey description places a tower at Appleby; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts marks it Removed and the Forest Fire Lookout Association index marks it Gone; no removal date found

events.note: Survey station description dated 1948 places a marker 25.0 feet southeast of the southeast leg of the Appleby fire tower, so a tower stood at Appleby by then

evidence.supports: Agency listed as the Texas Forest Service
Forest Lookouts page marks the tower as removed

evidence.quote: DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1948

evidence.supports: Marker located 25.0 feet southeast of the tower's southeast leg
evidence.quote: FIRE TOWER, 25.0 FEET SOUTHEAST OF THE SOUTHEAST LEG OF THE TOWER

evidence.supports: Town population nearly 1,000 during World War I
evidence.quote: At its height during World War I the town had a population of nearly 1,000
By the early 1950s the population had dwindled to 250
The post office was discontinued in 1958

evidence.supports: Index lists the tower as a Tower with status Gone

notes_for_editor: The 1948 station description is reproduced on the Forest Lookouts page; the original NGS datasheet was not opened. The Forest Lookouts page is the only source placing a tower at Appleby in 1948, so the date rests on that reproduction. A Texas A&M Forest Service archive item titled 'Forest Fire Protection-Steel Towers-Appleby Tower' (dated 1950s in the archive listing) appeared in search results but its page needs sign-in, so it was not read and is a lead only. The firelookout.org index misspells the county as Nacagdoches; the story uses Nacogdoches from the Forest Lookouts page. The Wikipedia Appleby article shows a water tower, not the lookout, so it is not used. Budget used: 2 WebSearch calls and about 6 page reads.
